doc.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jazz records, vaudeville and starting out
title: Records she heard: Kay Davis, Benny Goodman, Fletcher Henderson and Bechet
summary: She recalls records of Duke Ellington with Kay Davis, Benny Goodman tunes, Fletcher Henderson, Fred Astaire and Sidney Bechet.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I’m’a backtrack a little bit and just ask you two quick questions. There was a point where . . . it must have been a transition . . . where you started to learn to read the music, and also, what records did you have, when you talk about you were listening to Teddy Wilson, and the sister’s boyfriend had . . .
I remember we had . . .
. . . was playing some of his own recordings.
I remember we had things like Kay Davis singing with Duke, doing . . . what’s that thing she had? Was it called “Azure,” something like that?
Yeah, “Azure.”

I remember loving the vocal, singing way above the band. And then “Blue Goose” and . . . Those are two that stick in my mind. Then all the Benny Goodman things, like “Air Mail Special” and all the things that I got to play with the band later.
Fletcher Henderson arrangements, like . . . Edgar Sampson tunes, “Stomping at the Savoy”?
Yeah, yeah, yeah.
“Don’t Be That Way”? That kind of thing?
Yes, it seems like . . . that I’ve always known those tunes, always played them, never saw the music to them, they just . . .
Also, o.k., along those lines . . . So those were some of the records you had in your own personal collection, or someone had.
No, that he had.
You had access to . . .
I didn’t really . . .
Yeah.

I don’t know when I started getting a few records myself. I . . . There’s a grey area there in my brain. I just can’t think what I did. I remember having a record with Fred Astaire. As I think of it now, Fred Astaire probably was quite a good singer. A lot of people . . . I’m trying to remember what it was. It was like . . . what’s that thing? “Christopher Columbus.”
Yeah, that was by Fletcher Henderson’s band.

I just fell into hearing these things. I guess I automatically like the good things. I remember hearing . . . I liked it, but I don’t know why . . . hearing Sidney Bechet playing “Shake It But Don’t Break It” or “Shake It and Break It.” That was the name of the tune, “Shake It and Break It.” Boy, that’s going back a few years.
Yeah, I don’t know that one myself.
It was a blues-oriented thing. It had that rough barrelhouse sound. I liked those. I thought it was terrific. But I didn’t know why. I just liked it.
